title: Add validation that all targets used as platforms actually advertise

timeline.message:
Add validation that all targets used as platforms actually advertise
they provide PlatformInfo.

Fixes #10282.
timeline.author: John Cater

diff.patch:
@@ -1375,6 +1375,36 @@ EOF
   expect_log "Misconfigured toolchains: //:upper_toolchain is declared as a toolchain but has inappropriate dependencies"
 }
 
+
+# Catch the error when a target platform requires a configuration which contains the same target platform.
+# This can only happen when the target platform is not actually a platform.
+function test_target_platform_cycle() {
+  cat >> hello.sh <<EOF
+  #!/bin/sh
+  echo "Hello world"
+EOF
+  cat >> target.sh <<EOF
+  #!/bin/sh
+  echo "Hello target"
+EOF
+  chmod +x hello.sh
+  chmod +x target.sh
+  cat >> BUILD <<EOF
+sh_binary(
+  name = "hello",
+  srcs = ["hello.sh"],
+)
+sh_binary(
+  name = "target",
+  srcs = ["target.sh"],
+)
+EOF
+
+  bazel build --platforms=//:hello //:target &> $TEST_log && fail "Build succeeded unexpectedly"
+  expect_log "While resolving toolchains for target //:target: Target //:hello was referenced as a platform, but does not provide PlatformInfo"
+}

timeline.body: It might be useful to add a comment here why this exception cannot happen/can safely be ignored.
This map only seems to be used to create another collection out of its values. Consider merging the two stream operations and/or making this a set of package identifiers.

The owning class for this method is very strange - it's an AutoValue without fields? (Documentation would help!)

In any case this method should likely be static now and possibly live elsewhere so it can be used from here and its new usage properly.

reply.body: Moved and cleaned up the comment.
The AutoValue is present to give hashCode and equals implementations (needed for AutoCodec to work properly), and a toString. I can remove it and add simple versions of those, which is better?

timeline.message: Fix errorhandling and clean up tests.
timeline.author: John Cater

timeline.body: I don't quite understand why you don't return here if values are missing.

reply.body:
This is a source of many Skyframe errors: you have to propagate errors *before* you restart due to missing dependencies, or else the errors will be swallowed and either a) not ever be raised, or b) be raised for the parent of the current skyfunction call. Neither of these is good, and so checking for errors first is essential.

In the simple one-key `env.getValueOrThrow` case this happens automatically, because the `getValueOrThrow` method throws the error immediately and your exception handler catches it, but when requesting multiple keys at once via `env.getValuesOrThrow` it is surprisingly difficult to get it right.

This is why all of my skyfunctions have a lot of error-testing code, because I've been bitten by this too many times **and I still get it wrong the first time**.
Ugh. I'll reserve my rant about this for another time. :)

timeline.body: Can you also add a test for a missing platform target?
